headline: OpenAI has upgraded its ChatGPT Chrome extension so ChatGPT can read the tabs a user already has open and, in its Work mode, act on them.
score_reason: Product launch by a major company, stated by OpenAI; only a short article was available and no independent testing is reported.
importance_line: ChatGPT users who browse in Chrome can now ask the assistant to compare or manage their open tabs, which gives OpenAI's assistant more access to personal browsing, though the rollout details and safeguards were not described.
summary: The Verge reports that OpenAI has updated the ChatGPT extension for Google Chrome so that, when a user tags Chrome in the ChatGPT web or desktop app, the assistant can view the browser tabs already open, for example to compare three sofas a person is considering. The update also adds a fuller ChatGPT sidebar and lets ChatGPT Work, OpenAI's task-doing mode, control tabs to send messages, fill in forms or download files, similar to Google's Gemini-based "auto browse" feature.
notes: Short article (about 1,200 characters); a list of sample queries did not come through. No safeguards or availability details in the text.
